NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

SEP 25 1938

Two Terrorists Sentenced
Sorry Tale of Dud Bombs and Several Failures
For Which the Gangsters Were Punished

SENTENCES of twelve and seven years imprisonment respectively were imposed by Chief Judge Zee of the First Special District Court yesterday on Zao Sih-foong (alias Zau Dau Nyeu) and Wu Teh-fah (alias Siau Tung-tse), members of the pro-Japanese terrorist gang known as the "Yellow Way Society." Both Zao and Woo confessed to the bombing of the British-owned Chinese newspaper "Morning Leader," on the night of May 21, when a Chinese police constable and three others were injured.

Both men also confessed to having taken part in several other outrages and would-be outrages, and both said they received their instructions from 315-lb. Zang Nyoh-tsing, ex-convict and leader of the Hwang Tao Hui (Yellow Way Society) with headquarters in the New Asia Hotel.

With regard to the bombing of the "Morning Leader," Zao said that he received his bomb and his instructions from the terrorist society's headquarters in the New Asia Hotel and that the bomb was brought to the scene of action in the seat of a rickshaw.

Zao and his accomplice Wu presented a somewhat sorry spectacle as terrorists, for they admitted that on several occasions they were "stage struck" and unable to carry out Zang Nyoh-tsing's instructions. Zao and Wu themselves frequently were punished by the "society" they worked for not carrying out their "duties," Zao himself being tied up and imprisoned for several days on one occasion.

**Zao Punished**

According to the evidence produced by the police (including the confessions of the accused themselves), Zao threw a bomb from the Wing On Roof Garden down into crowded Chekiang Road on May 9; fortunately for the busy crowds, the missile failed to explode, and Zao was punished by the "Yellow Way Society" when he returned.

The next day, Zao again threw a bomb that failed to explode, this time outside the premises of the Central Trust Bureau, and once again he was punished.

On May 21, unfortunately for the British proprietors of the "Morning Leader," Zao had better luck for, after receiving his bomb from the Society's headquarters in the New Asia Hotel, he proceeded over the Szechuen Road bridge to the newspaper offices and there threw the grenade, which exploded and wounded four people.

**Zao, Wu Punished**

After a few week's rest, Zao and Wu were back on the job again, taking part in the wave of terrorism that broke over Shanghai on June 12, they told the police. Their particular job was the bombing of the Hwa Tung Broadcasting Station in Ningpo Road—but once again the bomb failed to go off and once again Zao and Wu were punished.

Then on June 19 came the attempt on the life of Mr. Su Ying-chi, president of the Ming Lee Middle School, Tifeng Road. Both Zao and Wu were together again in this would-be outrage and received their bombs and pistols at the "Yellow Way Society" branch headquarters, 86 Jessfield Road.

The attempt on Mr. Su's life was made near the school, but fortunately for their intended victim, Zao's nervous fingers were unable to pull the trigger and eventually Zao, Wu and two others ran away; they were punished severely by the Society.

The case against the two men closed on Wednesday, the case being adjourned for judgment. Yesterday morning, Chief Judge Zee sentenced Zao to twelve years' imprisonment, Wu to seven years.

1938年9月25日

两名恐怖分子被判刑
哑弹与数次失败的可悲故事
暴徒因此受惩

第一特区地方法院首席法官 Zee 昨日分别判处亲日恐怖团伙“黄道会”成员赵四丰（又名赵斗牛）和吴德发（又名萧童子）有期徒刑十二年和七年。赵、吴二人均供认于5月21日晚袭击英商中文报纸《导报》，致使一名华捕及另外三人受伤。

两人还供认参与其他几起暴行及未遂暴行，并称他们接受重达315磅的张耀庭（音译）的指令。张系前科犯，也是总部设在新亚酒店的“黄道会”首领。

关于袭击《导报》一事，赵称他从新亚酒店的恐怖组织总部领取炸弹并接受指令，炸弹被藏在人力车座位下运至行动现场。

作为恐怖分子，赵及其同伙吴的表现颇为可悲，因为他们承认有几次因“怯场”而未能执行张耀庭的指令。赵和吴本人常因未履行“职责”而受到其所效力的“会社”惩罚，赵有一次甚至被捆绑并囚禁数日。

**赵受惩处**

根据警方提供的证据（包括被告本人的供词），赵于5月9日从先施公司天台向拥挤的浙江路投掷了一枚炸弹；幸运的是，该爆炸物未爆炸，赵返回后受到“黄道会”的惩罚。

次日，赵再次投掷了一枚未爆炸的炸弹，这次是在中央信托局门外，他再次受到惩罚。

5月21日，《导报》的英方业主不幸遭遇了赵的“好运”，赵从新亚酒店的会社总部领取炸弹后，经由四川路桥前往报社办公室，投掷了手榴弹，炸弹爆炸，致四人受伤。

**赵、吴受惩处**

据二人向警方供述，休息几周后，赵和吴重新上岗，参与了6月12日爆发于上海的恐怖浪潮。他们的特定任务是轰炸宁波路的华东广播电台——但炸弹再次未能引爆，赵和吴再次受到惩罚。

随后在6月19日，发生了企图刺杀提丰路明理中学校长苏应之先生的案件。赵和吴再次共同参与了这起未遂暴行，并在极司菲尔路86号的“黄道会”分部总部领取了炸弹和手枪。

刺杀苏先生的行动发生在学校附近，但幸运的是，由于赵紧张的手指无法扣动扳机，最终赵、吴及另外两人逃跑了；他们受到了会社的严厉惩罚。

针对这两人的案件于周三审理终结，休庭待判。昨日上午，首席法官 Zee 判处赵有期徒刑十二年，吴有期徒刑七年。

JAPANESE DAILY PLACE BLAME
FOR TA PAO BOMBING

IN A SENSATIONAL
FEATURED REPORT, THE SHANGHAI MAINICHI YESTERDAY
CHARGED CHIANG KUANG-TANG, CHIEF EDITOR OF THE
TA PAO, WITH RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE BOMBING OF THE
NEWSPAPER ON MAY 21.

FIVE DAYS BEFORE THE
BOMBING, IN WHICH FOUR PEOPLE WERE INJURED, CHIANG,
ACCORDING TO THE JAPANESE DAILY, TOLD A
CHINESE JOURNALIST THAT HE HAD UNSUCCESSFULLY TRIED
TO OBTAIN A SUBSIDY FROM THE NATIONALIST GOVERNMENT.

"IF SOMEONE HURLS A
BOMB AT THE TAO PAO", HE WAS QUOTED AS SAYING, "IT
WILL BOTH GIVE GOOD PUBLICITY TO THE PAPER AND
CHANGE THE ATTITUDE OF THE NATIONALIST GOVERNMENT".

"IN VIEW OF THESE WORDS",
THE MAINICHI DECLARED, "THERE CAN BE NO DOUBT THAT
THE MORNING LEADER HAD ITSELF INVITED TERRORISTS TO
HURL BOMBS IN THE VICINITY OF ITS OFFICES".

日本日报将大炮轰炸归咎于人

在昨天一篇引人注目的专题报道中，《上海每日新闻》指控《导报》总编辑蒋光堂对5月21日的报纸遇炸事件负责。

据该日本日报称，在造成四人受伤的轰炸发生五天前，蒋曾对一名中国记者表示，他试图从国民政府获得补贴但未成功。

报道援引他的话说：“如果有人向《导报》投掷炸弹，这既能为报纸带来良好的宣传效果，又能改变国民政府的态度。”

《每日新闻》宣称：“鉴于这些言论，毫无疑问，《导报》是自己招引恐怖分子在其办公室附近投掷炸弹的。”

（续）

May 24, 1938. - 2 -

(1) 10 a.m. Vice-Admiral Oikawa
will inspect a naval parade on Kiangwan Road.
(2) 2 p.m. fencing and wrestling
matches will be held at Hongkew Park.
(3) 4.30 p.m. Lieutenant-Commander
Nakamura will deliver a lecture at the Japanese Club.
(4) 6.30 p.m. Japanese Naval Band
will give a concert and a moving picture will be screened
at the Japanese school on Range Road.

THE BOMBING INCIDENT NEAR THE "MORNING LEADER"

In connection with the bombing
incident on Ningpo Road near the office of the "Morning
Leader," a number of Chinese newspapers, especially the
"Morning Leader," spread a report to the effect that
certain Japanese were responsible for the bomb throwing
because the "Morning Leader" is a very anti-Japanese
paper.

According to information received
from a certain source, it was learned that five days
before the incident, Chiang Kwang-tang, chief editor of
the "Morning Leader," had stated to a certain Chinese
newspaper reporter that all the anti-Japanese newspapers
were receiving $5,000 to $6,000 every month from the
National Government for anti-Japanese activities, but the
"Morning Leader's" request for similar financial support
from the Government had been rejected. The "Morning
Leader" hoped that a certain person or party would
immediately throw a bomb at the paper so that the
Government might change its views.

It is, therefore, believed that
the bomb throwing must have been made by a certain anti-
Japanese element at the request of the paper itself.

Chiang Kwang-tang at one time
served with the "Livelihood Daily". At the beginning of
April he approached a small capitalist named Tang Ming-
shih and obtained financial assistance with which he
influenced a British subject named Sanders-Bates, Manager
of the University Press, Ltd., to lend his name for the
publication of the "Morning Leader" and for which he
was paid $300 a month by the paper.

30,000 CHINESE SOLDIERS TAKEN PRISONER

A Domei telegram from Tsinan dated
May 22 reports that 30,000 Chinese soldiers were taken
prisoner by the Japanese army at the fall of Hsuchow
and they are now being employed to transport food stuffs
and to repair the railways.

GENERAL CHANG SHIH-CHUNG REPORTED KILLED

A Domei telegram from Peking dated
May 23 reports that General Chang Shih-chung was killed
during the operations around Hsuchow.

(4) 下午6时30分，日本海军军乐队将在兰路日本学校举行音乐会并放映电影。

《导报》附近的轰炸事件

就宁波路《导报》办公室附近的轰炸事件而言，多家中文报纸，特别是《导报》，散布消息称某些日本人应对投掷炸弹负责，因为《导报》是一份非常反日的报纸。

据从某消息来源获悉的信息，事发五天前，《导报》总编辑蒋光堂曾对某中国报记者表示，所有反日报纸每月都从国民政府获得5,000至6,000美元用于反日活动，但《导报》要求政府提供类似财政支持的请求遭到拒绝。《导报》希望有人或某党派立即向报社投掷炸弹，以便政府改变看法。

因此，人们认为投掷炸弹一定是某些反日分子应报社自身要求所为。

蒋光堂曾就职于《立报》。4月初，他接触了一位名叫唐明士的小资本家，并获得经济资助，借此影响一位名为 Sanders-Bates 的英国臣民（大学印刷有限公司经理），让其出借名义出版《导报》，报社为此每月支付其300美元。

三万名中国士兵被俘

同盟通讯社5月22日从济南发出的电报称，徐州失守时，日军俘虏了三万名中国士兵，目前他们正被用于运输粮食和修复铁路。

张世忠将军 reportedly 阵亡

同盟通讯社5月23日从北平发出的电报称，张世忠将军在徐州周边的作战行动中阵亡。

Grenade Thrown at
Newspaper Office

Four Injured in Bombing
Of University Press,
130 Ningpo Road

Four people, including a woman
and a police constable, were injured
when terrorists struck again in the
Central District last night. A hand
grenade was thrown at about 10.35
p.m. outside the offices of the Univer-
sity Press Limited, a British firm of
publishers, at 130 Ningpo Road; the
premises houses the two Chinese-
language newspapers published by the
firm.

The sound of the explosion could
be heard clearly even as far away
as the Bund, where it was audible
above the clatter of the linotype
machines in the "North-China Daily
News" offices. If is not yet known
exactly how many men were in-
volved in the bombing, but it was
reported that either two or three
men, one of whom had thrown the
military-type hand grenade, were
present and that they then turned
and fled westwards down Ningpo
Road, past Honan Road.

The grenade tore a hole in the
pavement, smashed a window and the
glass in the doorway. It also gouged
large chips out of the walls of both
the publishing firm's building and of
the Kwang Hwa bank, on the op-
posite side of the road. Glass win-
dows on the ground floor of the bank
were smashed by fragments from the
bomb.

Three pedestrians—a Chinese wom-
an and two male Chinese—and Chi-
nese police constable No. 3318, on
duty not far off a were injured by
flying splinters and had to be rushed
to hospital by a Fire Brigade ambul-
ance, the woman to St. Elizabeth's,
where she was found to have sus-
tained wounds of the left arm, foot
and back; the two men to St. Luke's,
where they were found to have
suffered wounds to the forehead and
to the right thigh respectively; and
the constable to the Police Hospital,
with wounds in the left thigh and
right wrist.

Two "Riot Vans"

A large body of foreign and Chi-
nese detectives from Central Police
Station were soon on the scene, and
were reinforced by the combined
squads of two large "riot vans." The
entire area, for about a block each
way, was cordoned off and a search
conducted. The terrorists, however,
had made good their escape and no
arrests had been made up to the
time of going to press.

The University Press publishes the
"Morning Leader," or "Tao Pao,"
and the "News Digest," or "Mei
Jih-i Pao." Mr. J. A. E. Sanders-
Bates and Mr. N. E. Bonner, manag-
ing director and director of the
University Press respectively, were
soon on the scene and assisted a
"North-China Daily News" repre-
sentative in a tour of inspection of
the damage.

"We are coming out as usual to-
morrow," said Mr. Sanders-Bates.
Both he and Mr. Bonner were unable
to account for the bombing, since
they had always tried to avoid
political controversy.

1938年5月23日

手榴弹投向
报社办公室

大学印刷公司遇炸
四人受伤，
地址：宁波路130号

昨晚，恐怖分子再次在中央区作案，导致四人受伤，其中包括一名妇女和一名巡捕。晚上10点35分左右，一枚手榴弹被投掷到位于宁波路130号的英商出版机构大学印刷有限公司办公室外；该址设有该公司出版的两份中文报纸。

即使在远处的外滩也能清晰地听到爆炸声，那里的声音甚至盖过了《字林西报》办公室内莱诺铸排机的嘈杂声。目前尚不清楚确切有多少人参与了此次轰炸，但有报道称当时有两或三名男子在场，其中一人投掷了军用型手榴弹，随后他们转身沿宁波路向西逃跑，经过河南路。

手榴弹在人行道上炸出一个洞，震碎了一扇窗户和门口的玻璃。它还在出版公司大楼和马路对面的光华银行墙壁上凿出了大块碎片。银行的底层玻璃窗被炸弹碎片击碎。

三名行人——一名中国妇女和两名中国男子——以及在附近执勤的华捕第3318号，被飞溅的碎片击伤，并由救火会救护车紧急送往医院：该妇女被送往圣伊丽莎白医院，经查左臂、脚部和背部受伤；两名男子被送往圣路加医院，经查分别前额和右大腿受伤；该巡捕被送往警察医院，左大腿和右手腕受伤。

两辆“防暴车”

中央捕房的大量中外侦探很快赶到现场，并由两辆大型“防暴车”的联合小队增援。周围约一个街区的区域被封锁并进行搜查。然而，恐怖分子已成功逃脱，截至发稿时仍未逮捕任何人。

大学印刷公司出版《导报》（Tao Pao）和《每日新闻摘要》（Mei Jih-i Pao）。大学印刷公司的总经理 J. A. E. Sanders-Bates 先生和董事 N. E. Bonner 先生很快赶到现场，并协助《字林西报》代表视察受损情况。

“我们明天照常出版，” Sanders-Bates 先生说。他和 Bonner 先生都无法解释此次轰炸的原因，因为他们一直试图避免政治争议。

Chinese newspaper located at the
corner of Ningpo and Honan
Roads, was the target for a bomb
of the potato masher type, thrown
by an unknown man, who made
good his escape. Three Chinese
pedestrians, one of them a woman,
and a Chinese police constable
were injured. All four were detain-
ed in hospital last night.

The outrage took place a little
after 10.30 p.m. last night which was
rather fortunate, for, at an earlier
hour, the intersection is usually
crowded. Police, when informed of
the incident, rushed two riot vans
to the scene and conducted in-
vestigations on the spot, but little
information concerning the ident-
ity of the grenade thrower is
believed to have been elicited as
no one appears to have seen the
man toss the missile.

A Chinese constable is stationed
at the doors of the newspaper
office day and night, as a precau-
tion against just the type of out-
rage as was perpetrated last night.
Fragments of the bomb struck his
left thigh and wrist of the left hand.

Little damage was done to the
newspaper office itself. The explo-
sion broke most of the glass win-
dows of the building, but it only put
a brief halt to the activities of the
inmates, for, after the wreckage had
been cleared away, work was re-
sumed and the paper went to press
as usual.

No motive could be advanced for
the outrage.

在经历了10天的平静期后，恐怖活动于昨晚深夜再次显现，位于宁波路与河南路路口的一家中文报社《导报》（Tao Pao）或称《晨导报》（Morning Leader）的办公室成为一枚“土豆捣碎器”式炸弹的目标，该炸弹由一名身份不明的男子投掷，此人随后成功逃脱。三名中国行人（其中一人为女性）和一名华人巡捕受伤。四人昨晚均被留院治疗。

暴行发生在昨晚10点30分过后不久，这可谓不幸中的万幸，因为在较早的时间段，该十字路口通常拥挤不堪。警方获悉此事后，迅速派遣两辆防暴车赶赴现场并进行实地调查，但据信并未获得关于投弹者身份的任何线索，因为似乎无人看到该男子投掷爆炸物。

出于对昨晚这类暴行的防范，一名华人巡捕日夜驻守在报社门口。炸弹碎片击中了他的左大腿和左手手腕。

报社办公室本身受损甚微。爆炸震碎了大楼的大部分玻璃窗，但仅使内部人员的工作短暂中断，因为在清理废墟后，工作随即恢复，报纸也照常付印。

无法推断此次暴行的动机。

Four Wounded
In Bombing Of
Chinese Daily

British Edited Morning
Leader Is Target
Of Attack

One Chinese police constable,
attached to the Central Station,
and three Chinese pedestrians, one
woman and two men, were wound-
ed at 11 p.m. yesterday when an
unknown man hurled a potato-
masher type hand-grenade at the
printing offices of the Morning
Leader, a Chinese language daily
newspaper, situated at 130 Ningpo
Road.

The premises of the paper were
not damaged, the bomb hitting the
side of the wall near the entrance
and then bouncing to the sidewalk
before exploding.

The constable, who was standing
within four yards of where the
missile exploded, was wounded in
the thigh and wrist.

One of the pedestrians was
struck in the thigh, a serious
wound resulting. The other two
persons, including the woman, sus-
tained only slight injuries. All of
the wounded were taken to the
Lester Chinese Hospital. Two were
released after being given first aid
treatment.

Detectives Busy

Detectives of the Central Police
Station and a number of uniformed
men were rushed to the scene of
the bombing and Detective Sub-
Inspector Ovsannlakoff was still on
the job until an early hour this
morning investigating the affair.

The paper, at which the bomb
was thrown, is a recent addition to
the local newspaper field and is
published by a British subject, Mr.
J. A. E. Saunders-Bates, of the
University Press.

When the journal first made its
appearance several weeks ago, it
announced that its editorial policy
would be neutral and that it would
devote its pages to an unbiased
presentation of the news.

A headline, in red ink, appearing
in the Friday morning issue of the
paper reported that, according to
Chinese sources, Hsuchow had not
fallen and that some Japanese
troops were surrounded on a nearby
hill.

英人编辑的
《晨导报》成为

昨晚11时，一名隶属于中央捕房的华人巡捕以及三名中国行人（一男两女）受伤，当时一名身份不明的男子向位于宁波路130号的中文日报《晨导报》印刷所投掷了一枚“土豆捣碎器”式手榴弹。

报社场所未受损坏，炸弹击中入口附近的侧墙，随后弹至人行道上才爆炸。

该巡捕当时站在距离爆炸点四码以内，大腿和手腕受伤。

一名行人大腿中弹，伤势严重。另外两人（包括那名女性）仅受轻伤。所有伤者均被送往莱斯特长老会医院（Lester Chinese Hospital）。两人在接受急救处理后获释。

侦探忙碌中

中央捕房的侦探及多名制服警员被紧急派往爆炸现场，副探长奥夫桑尼拉科夫（Ovsannlakoff）一直工作至今日凌晨早些时候，对此事进行调查。

遭到投弹袭击的这份报纸是本地报业的新成员，由大学书局（University Press）的英籍人士 J. A. E. 桑德斯-贝茨（J. A. E. Saunders-Bates）先生出版。

该刊物于数周前首次面世时曾宣布，其编辑方针保持中立，并将致力于客观公正地呈现新闻。

在该报周五早版中，一条用红墨水印刷的标题报道称，据中方消息来源，徐州并未陷落，且部分日军被包围在附近的一座山丘上。

At 10.35p.m. on May 21st a telephone message
was received at the station from C.P.C. 1261 to the
effect that a hand-grenade had been thrown on the
Ningpo Road near the Honan Road and several persons
had been injured.
On receipt of the said telephone message at
the station, C.D.S. 312 and the undersigned
immediately proceeded to the scene of the crime
and carried out thorough examination of the road
outside the office of the newspapers and also made
enquiries among the by-standers and watchmen. From
enquiries made it appears that at about 10.20p.m.
on May 21st an unknown person threw a hand-grenade
of 'potato masher' type into the front door of
Chinese newspaper "Morning Leader" and "News Digest"
published by Mr. J.A.E. Sanders-Bates, British,
and Mr. N.E. Bonner, British, former employee of
the S.M.P.
It appears that the thrower was evidently on
the southern side of the Ningpo Road and threw the
bomb aiming at the front door but misjudged the
distance with the result that the bomb struck the
corner of a wall at the door and fell on the foot-
path about 2 yards to the east of the front door
and exploded. At the time of explosion a party of
5 male Chinese and one woman had been passing along
the Ningpo Road from east to west. They just
passed the front door of the newspapers office when
the explosion occurred. A man named Tia Tsang Sung

Clerk Woo Chen I.
Central Stn. 21-5-38

States:-
At about 10.20p.m. 21/5/38 I was on duty at the "Morning
Leader" Newspaper Office, 13C Ningpo Road. Whilst I was standing
near the entrance of Ching Zung Li, about 6-7 yards east of the
front door of the newspaper office, there were only a few
pedestrians on the road, and suddenly I observed a man in dark
foreign clothing together with 2 or 3 others wearing dark
long gowns (owing to darkness no further description are available)
walk along the south side footpath in a westerly direction.
When they came near a black m/car, which had been parked on the
opposite side of the newspaper Office, I heard a noise sounded
as if something dropping on the ground, outside the front door
of the newspaper office. Not knowing that it was a bomb I
thought something might have fallen down from the top of the
building, and when I looked up I did not see any light in the
windows. At this moment I suddenly heard a great noise of
explosion and fell to the ground unconscious, being wounded by
the bomb explosion. I did not know what happened to those above
mentioned pedestrians. A few minutes later I regained my senses
and was conveyed to the Police Hospital by an ambulance which
had been called by Police officers who had come to the scene.
The above is my true statement.

Crossmarked By: Yuan Sih Tsia.

手榴弹可能是为了恐吓附近的修车行老板而投掷的，因为侦探注意到最近几周有几辆日本拥有的汽车在那里维修，但对此的调查未能证实这一点。

1938年5月10日上午10时，接到宝隆医院的电话报告，称名为翟陈氏的女子因在轰炸中受伤，于同日早上9时在该院死亡。

At 7.53 p.m. on 7/5/38 a telephone message was received at Sinza Station from C.P.C. 2025 reporting that a bomb had exploded in a garbage bin off Avenue Road West of Carter Road and that several persons had been injured.

S.F.B. Emergency Ambulance was called, and all available men under Inspector Perkins, Officer i/c attended immediately. The Reserve Unit under Assistant Commissioner Fairbairn and C/Inspector Lovell also attended the scene.

The following persons were transferred to the Paulun Hospital by Ambulance:-

(1) Tsih Zung Sz (翟陈氏), m/female, aged 44, native of Chingkiang, residing No. 6 Kyung Yih Li, Kaifeng Road. Doctor's Certificate reads: "Wound on spine, fragment not extracted. Wound on buttock, not extracted. Serious".

(2) Tsih Ying Sung (翟應元), aged 52, Chingkiang, Earthenware dealer, No. 6 Kyung Yih Li, Kaifeng Road. Doctor's chit reads:- "Wound on lower right arm and on right lower leg." Not detained.

爱文义路手榴弹爆炸案。

1938年5月7日晚上7时53分，新闸巡捕房接到华捕第2025号的电话报告，称在卡特路以西的爱文义路西段路边的一个垃圾箱内发生炸弹爆炸，数人受伤。

消防队紧急救护车被召出，由负责警官珀金斯 (Perkins) 督察率领的所有可用警力立即赶赴现场。由副局长费尔贝恩 (Fairbairn) 和洛弗尔 (Lovell) 总督察率领的后备队也赶到了现场。

以下人员由救护车送往宝隆医院：-

(1) 翟陈氏 (Tsih Zung Sz)，女，44岁，镇江籍，居住开封路京义里6号。医生证明书写道：“脊柱伤口，碎片未取出。臀部伤口，未取出。重伤”。

(2) 翟应元 (Tsih Ying Sung)，52岁，镇江籍，陶器商，居住开封路京义里6号。医生便条写道：“右前臂和右小腿伤口。” 未留院。

第1和第2项为夫妻关系。

(3) 潘阿荣 (Peu Ah Yoong)，32岁，浦东籍，木匠，居住？大沽路。医生便条写道：“右大腿伤口，碎片仍在体内。不严重。” 留院治疗。

爆炸现场是爱文义路南侧、卡特路以西约200码处的一块空地，这块空地上有两个车库，每个车库都停放着一辆私人汽车。公共工部局的一个垃圾箱也在这块空地内，空地后面有一堵矮墙，如果不是有一条短巷穿过锁闭式车库和墙后，这里本是一个死胡同。

An examination showed a small hole in the cement
to the West side of the dust-bin, numerous dents in the
low wall and in an old motor car parked on the land.
Near the scene of the explosion were found two wooden
splinters, similar to that of bombs of the "Potato Masher"
type. Six cast-iron fragments were also found.
C.P.C. 2025 when questioned stated that he had been
on duty at the corner of Carter Road and Avenue Road and
that he had run to the scene when he heard the explosion.
He had seen the injured persons sitting or lying on the
pavement and had then called the Station by telephone.
C.D.S. 72 and the undersigned visited the Paulun
Hospital and questioned the injured persons, but they
were unable to give any useful information, they having
been injured when passing the scene of the explosion.
The wall at the rear of the Dust-bin in the North
boundary of the Hu Kwang (沪光) Middle School, Lane
41, No. 48-50 Carter Road. This School was visited by
detectives and the Principal, Mr. Lieu Sah Ching (盧石青)
was questioned. the following information being obtained:-
About 200 students are enrolled there, their ages
being between 12 years and 20 years. Only seven students
resideson the premises.
A window on the first floor, about 18 feet from the
ground, was broken, either by fragments of the grenade of
by the concussion. No persons were injured inside the
School.

经检查，发现垃圾桶西侧的水泥地面上有一个小洞，低矮的围墙以及停放在该地块上的一辆旧汽车上有多处凹痕。在爆炸现场附近发现了两块木制碎片，与“土豆捣碎器”式手榴弹的木柄相似。还发现了六块铸铁碎片。
中央巡捕房警员第 2025 号在接受询问时称，他当时正在卡特路（Carter Road）与爱文义路（Avenue Road）拐角处执勤，听到爆炸声后跑向现场。他看到伤者坐在或躺在人行道上，随后通过电话向警局报告。
侦探警佐第 72 号及本人前往宝隆医院（Paulun Hospital）询问了伤者，但他们未能提供任何有用信息，因为他们是在经过爆炸现场时受伤的。
上述垃圾桶位于卡特路 48-50 号、41 弄沪光中学北界后方。侦探人员走访了该校，并询问了校长卢石青先生（Lieu Sah Ching），获得如下信息：
该校注册学生约 200 名，年龄在 12 岁至 20 岁之间。仅有七名学生住在校内。
一楼的一扇窗户破损，该窗距地面约 18 英尺，系被手榴弹碎片或冲击波震碎。校内无人受伤。

The Principal was questioned, but was unable to
give any information which would suggest that the missile
was thrown with the intention of intimidating him or any
of his staff. He states that he has not received any
threatening letters and that he does not deal in politics.
There are nine tenants in the School buildings,
as follows:-
(1) Sung Foh Yeu (陈福元), clerk employed in the
Central Savings Society.
(2) Bang Kyung Meu (彭金茂), Analyst, temporarily
unemployed.
(3) Tseu Sing Ziang (周新祥), Fur Store Assistant,
Honan Road.
(4) Liang Tsang Sz (梁張氏), m/female, husband at
present absent in Hongkong, being employed
as a cook.
(5) Wong Bein Ling (黄培林), clerk attached to
Louza Police Station.
(6) Yih Zung Sz (叶陳氏), m/female, independent.
(7) Lieu Poh Yien (刘博淵), clerk employed in Central
Bank of China.
(8) Wong Kyung Zang (黄慶長), clerk employed in the
Mercantile Bank of India.
(9) Liang Vung Seu (梁文瑞), clerk employed in
A.P.C.

All of these persons were questioned, but could
not supply any information likely to assist in investiga-
tions.

Despite thorough enquiries on the scene, no
witnesses to the actual bombing could be found, and the
motive is still obscure, although it is possible that the
object was to intimidate the Principal of the School, for
some reason not desclosed by him.

(2) 彭金茂（Bang Kyung Meu），化验师，暂时失业。
(3) 周新祥（Tseu Sing Ziang），河南路皮草店店员。
(4) 梁張氏（Liang Tsang Sz），女，丈夫目前在香港受雇担任厨师，不在身边。
(5) 黄培林（Wong Bein Ling），罗致警察局（Louza Police Station）附属职员。
(6) 叶陳氏（Yih Zung Sz），女，无业/独立生活。
(7) 刘博淵（Lieu Poh Yien），中国银行职员。
(8) 黄慶長（Wong Kyung Zang），印度商业银行（Mercantile Bank of India）职员。
(9) 梁文瑞（Liang Vung Seu），A.P.C. 公司职员。

上述人员均接受了询问，但未能提供可能有助于调查的任何信息。

尽管在现场进行了彻底查访，但未能找到目睹实际爆炸过程的证人，作案动机仍不明确，尽管有可能是出于某种未向校方透露的原因，意图恐吓该校校长。
